long.vo: Two hundred and ninety-eight crore rupees. Sixty-six slots. Ten teams. One auction, on the sixteenth of December, in गोवा. Before a single bid, we looked at what each squad is missing.

scene.tagline: What every IPL team still needs

long.vo: Here is how. We took every squad as it stands today: retained players, plus trades. Then we measured, from two seasons of ball-by-ball data, how many balls those players face and bowl in each phase. A hundred percent is an average squad. Below seventy is a hole.

scene.kicker: OUR MODEL · IPL 2025-26 · IN OUR ARCHIVE

long.vo: First, the money. लखनऊ have the most, forty-seven point four five crore, for seven slots. कोलकाता, forty-one. हैदराबाद, forty. दिल्ली, thirty-nine, with nine slots to fill. Then मुंबई, चेन्नई, राजस्थान. पंजाब have eighteen. बेंगलुरु, fourteen. And गुजरात, under nine crore, for three slots.

Put it all in one grid, and the picture is clear. Pace is the league's biggest hole, at the death and with the new ball. Spin is thin at मुंबई and हैदराबाद. And कोलकाता are thin almost everywhere. Let's go through them, most needy first.

scene.kicker: CAPACITY VS AN AVERAGE SQUAD (1.00) · OUR MODEL, IPL 2025-26
scene.title: The need map.

long.vo: कोलकाता. Batting is thin in every phase. Powerplay, forty-six percent of average. Middle overs, sixty-one. Death overs, sixty-five. Only one wicketkeeper, and pace at sixty percent. forty-one point six five crore, three overseas slots, and a long list.
चेन्नई. Pace is the hole. forty-eight percent in the powerplay, forty-nine at the death. Death batting is thin too, at sixty-seven. twenty-eight point zero five crore, six slots, two overseas.

दिल्ली. Their openers are at forty-six percent. Pace is the problem in both phases: fifty-six in the powerplay, forty-five at the death. thirty-nine point five crore, and the most overseas slots in the league, four.
लखनऊ have the biggest purse, and the clearest need. Pace, at both ends. forty-six percent with the new ball, forty-three at the death. Batting at the death is a little short too, at seventy-seven.
हैदराबाद. Spin is at forty-five percent, and the powerplay batting, which drives their whole approach, is at sixty. forty point one five crore says they can fix both.

पंजाब. The issue is not how much, but how well. Their pace bowlers go for ten point six runs an over in the powerplay, and eleven point eight at the death. The league's are nine point three, and ten point four. eighteen point six crore, six slots.
मुंबई. A strong squad with one hole: spin, at forty-two percent of average. A wrist-spinner is the missing piece, and thirty-two point six crore can buy one.

राजस्थान are balanced. Their powerplay batting strikes at one eighty-seven, the best in the league. बेंगलुरु are balanced too, with fourteen crore and five slots. And गुजरात are the deepest squad of all, with three slots and under nine crore. They will be watching, not shopping.

Now, who is out there? The registered list comes around the third of December, so this is only the players the teams released. Pace is rich: Trent Boult, मथीशा पथिराना, दीपक चाहर. Spin is thin: वानिन्दु हसरंगा, then very little. Openers: पथुम निसंका. And finishers are the thinnest market of all.

So who could draw the biggest bids? This is our model, an opinion, not a price prediction. Trent Boult: good in the powerplay and the death, and four teams with over a hundred and fifty crore between them could want him. मथीशा पथिराना: the best death bowler on the market. वानिन्दु हसरंगा: the only proven wrist-spinner, and both मुंबई and हैदराबाद need spin. दीपक चाहर: an Indian new-ball bowler, no overseas slot needed. पथुम निसंका: the best realistic opener.

long.title: IPL 2027 Auction Preview: What Every Team Needs | Data Story Ep 15
long.description:
IPL 2027 auction preview: what every IPL team needs. Ten squads, ₹298 crore, 66 slots, one auction on 16 December 2026 in Goa. We measured each squad's batting by phase and its pace and spin from IPL 2025-26 ball-by-ball data, then matched the gaps to the players the franchises released.

In our model Kolkata are thin in every phase; Chennai, Delhi and Lucknow need pace; Hyderabad and Mumbai need spin; Punjab's pace is expensive; Rajasthan, Bengaluru and Gujarat are balanced. Boult, Pathirana, Hasaranga, Chahar and Nissanka could draw the biggest bids (opinion, not a price prediction).

Purses and slots as of 17 November 2026, not yet official. The registered list is due around 3 December; Starc and Head are reported unavailable. Capacity: 100% is an average squad. Our model, in our archive (Sportmonks IPL 2025-26).
